title: Safety-net GeoRouter: skew-aware quantile fusion + link-fidelity signatures
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a safety-net GeoRouter component that selects region and tier using skew-aware fusion of p50/p95 latency signals together with a compact network link-fidelity signature. The goal is to provide robust region selection that avoids noisy short-term spikes and degrades gracefully to fallback model variants when either latency or link fidelity indicate sustained degradation.
acceptance_criteria: GeoRouter computes a composite score per region using configurable weights for p50, p95, and a link-fidelity metric
Router exposes an API to return an ordered list of candidate regions + preferred model variant for each region
Decision logic includes hysteresis & skew-detection to prevent flip-flopping for transient p95 spikes
End-to-end simulation harness shows reduced cross-region failovers in synthetic jitter/packetloss scenarios compared to baseline routing
Unit and integration tests for score calculation, hysteresis windows, and fallback selection are added
Document rollout and rollback plan; console dashboard shows per-region scoring components (p50, p95, link-fidelity)
design_decisions: Use EWMA-backed percentile smoothing for p50/p95 inputs with separate decay constants to capture short/long signals
Compute link-fidelity as a compact score derived from packet-loss, RTT variance, and TCP retransmit events; treat as orthogonal to latency percentiles
Fuse signals via a weighted linear combination, but add a multiplicative penalty term when link-fidelity < threshold to rapidly demote affected regions
Detect skew when p95 - p50 > skew_threshold and apply a conservative penalty to the region's score to prefer lower-skew options for latency-sensitive customers
Hysteresis: require N consecutive scoring ticks below/above thresholds before changing primary region; support staged canary switchover for traffic-sensitive tenants
Fallback model variant selection prioritizes same-architecture quantized variants in the same region before cross-region model fallbacks to minimize data movement
tradeoffs_and_risks: Linear fusion is simple and explainable but may underweight rare catastrophic link events — mitigated by multiplicative penalty and hard cutoffs
Aggressive hysteresis reduces flapping but increases time to recover post-incident; we will tune via staged experiments and SLO impact analysis
Computing link-fidelity requires additional telemetry and cardinality; initial implementation will reuse existing edge metrics pipelines to avoid a new ingestion tier
Fallbacking to quantized model variants may change output quality; we will attach QA prompts and monitor regeneration divergence metrics during rollouts
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Prototype scoring library in Rust (shared with serving runtime) and a feature-flagged GeoRouter endpoint that returns scores only
Phase 2 (3 wks): Integrate telemetry inputs (p50/p95 streams + link events) and add hysteresis state machine; unit tests and simulation harness
Phase 3 (2 wks): Add fallback model variant logic, tie into route decision API, and integration tests with request routing simulator
Phase 4 (2 wks): Canary rollout to internal tenants, collect metrics (failovers, request latency distribution, model quality diffs), iterate weights
Phase 5 (1 wk): Documentation, console dashboard tiles, alerts, and runbook updates

notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the multiplicative penalty design — it should be aggressive enough to demote regions with poor link-fidelity but avoid false positives on short blips.
We plan to run A/B experiments vs current region selection for 2 weeks of traffic; provide guidance on experiment metrics (p99 tail, failover count, quality regression).
The proposal uses a small number of tunable knobs. We'll add a self-service UI for tenant-level overrides later (out of scope for initial rollout).
final_notes: This ticket is part of a broader effort to make routing decisions more telemetry-resilient and to codify safe fallback semantics for model variants. Keep early rollouts limited to non-critical tenants and collect both latency and quality signals before wider deployment.
